title: The Year of the Four Emperors
objective: After this level you can explain what happened in 69 CE and what it revealed about imperial power.
summary: In 69 CE four men ruled in turn, each backed by an army. Vespasian won, proving that emperors could be made far from Rome.

cards.headline: In a single year, Rome had four emperors.
cards.body: Nero was dead, and Augustus’ family line with him. So who got to rule now? Whoever had an army behind him.

cards.headline: 69 CE
cards.body: After Nero’s death in 68 CE came 69 CE, the Year of the Four Emperors. Galba, Otho, Vitellius and Vespasian each held power in turn. Four names, one calendar. What they had in common was an army: each claimant was backed by one. That was the year’s real lesson. The legions could make emperors, and they could unmake them.

mascot.line: This is Level 32’s idea again: armies loyal to their generals, now choosing emperors.

cards.headline: The winner
cards.body: The last man standing was Vespasian, a general commanding in Judaea. He won the civil war and founded the Flavian dynasty. Looking back at Nero’s fall, the historian Tacitus named what it had exposed, a secret of empire: an emperor could be made somewhere other than Rome. The top job no longer had to be decided in the capital. It could march in from far away.

cards.fact: Vespasian came from a family of modest rank.
cards.context: No old Roman nobility, no famous ancestors. What he had was an army, and in 69 CE that counted for more than an ancient name.

questions.prompt: Who won the civil war of 69 CE?
questions.explanation: Vespasian won and founded the Flavian dynasty.

questions.prompt: What did 69 CE reveal about imperial power?

options.label: The Senate could choose emperors freely
Armies far from Rome could make emperors
Only Nero’s family could ever rule
Emperors had to be born in Rome

questions.explanation: Each claimant had an army behind him, and the winner was proclaimed in the provinces.

questions.prompt: From Level 32: why would legions back their own general for emperor?

options.label: The Senate ordered each legion to vote
Generals were chosen by soldiers each year
Soldiers looked to their general for their future
The emperor had stopped paying the legions

questions.explanation: Since Marius, soldiers depended on their commander for pay and land, so their loyalty followed him.
